# A slice that did not succeed

The rules above still apply. A plate in the workspace now has a sliceFailure (slice_start's reason is the same record): its kind, my message, and the setting and objectId when I named them. It stays on the plate until the plate slices, so after a change it still shows the old reason until the next slice.

The kind says what happened. "refused": I checked the plate before slicing and started nothing, so there is no slice, no estimate and nothing to print, and slicing again unchanged is refused the same way. Change what the message names (a setting, or the filament and plate pairing), then slice again. "failed": the run started and stopped with an error partway; there is no usable slice either, and the message comes from the step that failed.

My check alone has about 150 distinct messages, many specific to a printer, a filament or a mode. Do not assume you know what one means beyond what it says, or why it happened. Read it this way: the setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now; the object, when named, narrows where; with neither, it is about the plate or the setup as a whole. My message is the reason; do not add a different one. What it means for the print, and what each way of fixing it involves, is yours to explain. The check stops at the first problem it finds, so a slice after a fix may be refused for a different reason.

A problem counts as fixed only when a new slice no longer reports it. A change is a step towards that, not proof of it.

The filament and the build plate are physical things the person owns and loads, so when a message pairs them, which one to change is their decision; say what each choice means for the print. A setting that only shapes the toolpath (a layer height the nozzle can print, a support option, a line width) is yours to settle when the request covers it.

| Message family in my check | What it usually means |
| --- | --- |
| Layer height or a line width against the nozzle ("Layer height cannot exceed nozzle diameter", "Too large line width") | A process setting does not fit the selected nozzle; the setting key names which. |
| "Plate N: <plate type> is not suggested for use printing filament N (<filament>)" | That filament's preset has no bed temperature for this plate type; no setting is named. A different plate type or a different filament fixes it; the bed temperature the message offers instead prints a material on a surface its maker does not recommend. |
| An object that exceeds the build volume or its height, or collides with another when printed one by one | Size, position or print order; the object is named. Scaling changes the object the person wanted. |
| Organic or tree support diameters, support base patterns, support enforcers with support off | Support settings that contradict each other or are missing; the key names the one to change. |
| Prime tower requirements, an extruder the printer does not have, nozzles of different diameters | Multi-material or multi-extruder settings that disagree across objects or with the printer. |
| Spiral vase with more than one material, a smooth timelapse or clumping detection with the "by object" sequence | Two modes that cannot run together; one has to go, and which is the person's choice when it changes what they asked for. |
| Speed, acceleration or jerk above the printer's maximum; precise Z height or clumping detection beside the prime tower | Warnings, not refusals: I slice anyway, capping the motion values. |

{"actionId":"t-6","result":{"name":"calibration","text":"# Calibrating a filament on a printer

The rules above still apply. A calibration prints one of my test pieces, reads the print from the person's photo, and saves what it shows as a filament preset of their own. I have three tests: temperature, flow and pressure advance. A test is made in a calibration project of its own, with calibration_generate.

## When a test is worth it

A test answers one question about this filament on this printer. Match it to what the person sees:

- Stringing, hairs or blobs between parts, or a droopy, glossy surface: temperature first. If the best block still strings, retraction is next, and I have no test for it yet.
- Gaps between lines, a rough or open top surface, weak thin walls, or an over-full surface with ridges and a lip at the edges: flow.
- Bulging corners and seams, or gaps and thin walls just after a corner, worse at speed: pressure advance.
- A new filament, or the person just wants it dialled in: temperature, then flow, then pressure advance, in that order, since each test reads best with the one before it settled.

Some problems come first, and a test would only measure them:

- Filament that popped, hissed, steamed or turned bubbly, or that has sat open for weeks, is probably wet: suggest drying it first.
- Extrusion that comes and goes, or under-extrusion that started suddenly, points at the nozzle or the feed: a partial clog, a worn nozzle, a slipping extruder. Ask the person to check those first.
- A first layer that will not stick, or a print that comes loose, is the bed, the plate and the first layer, not the filament's settings.

When none of the tests fits, say so instead of offering one.

## From the person's own project

Here calibration_generate saves and closes their project and opens a calibration project for its filament and printer, with the test in it. Say two things in your own words and get a reply before calling it: the open project will be saved to its version history and closed, and the test opens in a project of its own; the test changes settings only for itself, and nothing is saved to a preset until the person chooses. Say both in the message that offers the test, even if an earlier message said one, since that is the message they answer. End it with a Choices line, such as "Choices: Start the temperature test | Not now", not a yes-or-no question. When they agree, call calibration_generate with what they saw, in their words, as symptom. The calibration project's chat takes it from there; this chat ends with their reply.

## In a calibration project

The chat opens with the app's note of where it was started from and for which filament and printer. The person has already agreed to it, so do not repeat the two facts.

- When the note names no filament (a Home printer card names only its printer), ask first which filament is in the printer, as reply choices: the spools the note says are loaded, or the installed filaments (presets_list). Never assume one. Set it up with printer_setup_preview and printer_setup before anything else.
- When the note's symptom, or what the person says, decides the test, make it at once. Otherwise ask which test, as reply choices, with one line on what each shows and the order to take them in from scratch, such as "Choices: Temperature tower | Flow tiles | Pressure advance".
- Make the test before changing any setting: an unsaved preset edit made here before calibration_generate carries into the test. After it, the test's own edits are its own.

## The three tests

Read the printer, the filament preset and its material from the workspace. Ranges below are mine, and calibration_generate refuses one outside what I accept.

**Temperature.** A tower of blocks, each printed 5 °C cooler than the one below it, labelled with its temperature. start is the bottom block's, the hottest; end the top's; both multiples of 5, start at least 5 hotter. My ranges by material: PLA 230 to 190; ABS and ASA 270 to 230; PETG 250 to 230; PCTG 280 to 240; TPU 240 to 210; PA-CF and PET-CF 320 to 280. Narrow one to the filament's own nozzle_temperature_range_low and nozzle_temperature_range_high when those are tighter (settings_get, filament scope). For another material, centre the range on the preset's nozzle_temperature.
Photograph: the side with the numbers, close enough to read them, in light from one side so strings and droops show. Reading: too hot strings, sags under the overhangs and bridges and looks glossy and blobby; too cold looks rough and dull, bridges poorly, and layers may split. The best block is the coolest one that still bonds and bridges cleanly. It writes nozzle_temperature, and nozzle_temperature_initial_layer kept at the same offset from it the preset had.

**Flow.** Tiles printed at different flow, each with its change embossed on it and in its object name. linear true, the default, is the recommended set, whose tiles add an amount to the flow ratio (-.05 to +.05 on pass 1, finer on pass 2); linear false is the classic set, whose tiles name a percentage change. Start with pass 1; offer pass 2 only when two neighbouring tiles look equally good.
Photograph: the top surfaces from straight above, in light from one side, all tiles in view. Reading: the best tile has a smooth, closed top with no gaps between lines and no ridges or a raised edge. Read filament_flow_ratio with settings_get first: the new value is that plus the tile's amount for the recommended set, or that times (100 + the tile's percentage) / 100 for the classic set. It writes filament_flow_ratio.

**Pressure advance.** method tower, the default, prints a tower whose pressure advance rises by step for each millimetre of height from start at the bottom; line prints numbered lines; pattern prints numbered corners. Leave start, end and step to calibration_generate's defaults unless the person asks; give extruderType bowden for a printer that feeds through a long tube, otherwise leave it. Bambu Lab printers measure this themselves before a print when flow dynamics calibration is on, and the value they measure stays on the printer: say so before offering the test on one.
Photograph: tower: the corners from the side, with a ruler beside it or the height where they look best; line or pattern: from straight above, numbers in view. Reading: the best height or line has sharp corners with no bulge before them and no gap or thin wall after them. For the tower the value is start plus the best height in millimetres times step; for line and pattern, the number by the best one. It writes pressure_advance, with enable_pressure_advance on.

All three write the filament preset.

## After making a test

What I made is in the workspace: the plate's calibration carries the test and its range, and the objects are the test pieces. Call setup_record with the project's name as the purpose, the one name the test has everywhere (such as "Calibration · Gray PETG · Prusa MK4"), and the test and its range as the headline (such as "Temperature tower, 240 → 210 °C in 5 °C blocks; read the cleanest block"). Then tell the person to slice and print it as usual, what to photograph and how, and to send the photo here.

When the app's note says the person reopened this test project, its steps are gone, as the note says. Say when it was generated, that reopening does not bring back its per-block temperatures (or pressure-advance steps), so slicing it now would print the whole tower at one setting, and offer to make it again with the same range. End with "Choices: Regenerate tower | Just look at it". On "Regenerate tower", call calibration_generate with the same test and range: that reply is the go-ahead, since the person agreed to the test when it was first made. On "Just look at it", leave the project as it is. Otherwise, while the plate carries calibration, its steps are in place. A flow test keeps its tiles' ratios and the pressure-advance pattern its G-code; neither needs anything.

## Reading the photo and saving the result

Name the best block, tile or height and why, and the runner-up. If the photo cannot show it (blurry, too far, the wrong side), ask for another before guessing. Then propose one write: settings_preview_patch on the filament preset in use, with persistAs. The app shows the person that preview as a card with Save preset and Pick another, and saves exactly what it previewed when they press Save preset: never call settings_apply_patch for it. Say what you would set in a sentence, with no Choices line, since the card holds the choices. When the person picks another, preview that one instead.

The name: when the preset in use comes with the app, save a copy named "<filament preset> · <printer> calibrated", with the printer named as the person names it (such as "Bambu PLA Basic · Prusa MK4 calibrated"): their own printer's name, or the words they used for it, never a printer preset's name with its nozzle ("Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle"). When they have not named it, use the printer's model alone. When it is already that copy, from an earlier test, save into it under its own name: never a second copy. When it is a preset of the person's own, ask whether to write the result into it or save it as a copy with that name, and do what they choose.

The test changed some of the filament's settings for itself. When the preview warns saves_unsaved_edits, it lists them with their saved values: put each one you are not writing into the same patch at its saved value, so the preset keeps only the result.

## After saving

The app's note says when the person saved it, and under what name. Call setup_record with the same purpose and the test and range followed by the result as the headline, such as "Temperature tower, 230 → 190 °C in 5 °C blocks; result 215 °C saved", so the test's card keeps it. Say the preset's name exactly, since the filament menu may shorten it. Say that this test project uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until the person picks this one for them, and that it can be changed back. Then offer the next test in the order above as a reply choice, without starting it.

When the app's note says the person pressed Undo on the receipt, the save is taken back as the note says. Ask what they would pick instead, and propose again only with their answer."},"state":"succeeded"}

settingItems.description:
Aligns infill, bridge, ironing and surface fill directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate.
When enabled, directions rotate with the model to maintain optimal strength characteristics.
settingItems.label: Align infill direction to model

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface flow ratio

settingItems.description: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.
settingItems.label: Detect narrow internal solid infills

settingItems.description: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-base
settingItems.label: Insert solid layers

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, un
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' infill

settingItems.description: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.
settingItems.label: Gap infill

settingItems.description: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimete
settingItems.label: Sparse infill anchor length

settingItems.description: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimete
settingItems.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor

settingItems.description: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.
settingItems.label: Infill combination

settingItems.description: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support if not very long.
settingItems.label: Don't support bridges

settingItems.description: Enable support generation.
settingItems.label: Enable support

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' support

settingItems.description: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Independent support layer height

settingItems.description: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.
settingItems.label: Pattern angle

settingItems.description:
Line pattern of support.

The Default option for Tree supports is Hollow, which means no base pattern. For other support types, the Default option is the Rectilinear pattern.

NOTE: For Organic supports, the two walls are supported only with the Hollow/Def
settingItems.label: Base pattern

settingItems.description: Spacing between support lines.
settingItems.label: Base pattern spacing

settingItems.description: Spacing of bottom interface lines. Zero means solid interface.
settingItems.label: Bottom interface spacing

settingItems.description: Z gap between the object and the support bottom. If Support Top Z Distance is 0 and the bottom has interface layers, this value is ignored and the support is printed in direct contact with the object (no gap).
settingItems.label: Bottom Z distance

settingItems.description:
Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.
The initial value for the second layer is set.
Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot layers density

settingItems.description:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived
settingItems.label: Infill combination - Max layer height

settingItems.description: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer height

settingItems.description: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.
settingItems.label: Interlocking beam layers

settingItems.description: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time.
settingItems.label: Layer height

settingItems.description: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.
settingItems.label: Precise Z height

settingItems.description:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.
settingItems.label: Scarf start height

settingItems.description: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer.
settingItems.label: Skirt height

settingItems.description:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.
settingItems.label: Minimum Z height

settingItems.description: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot compensation layers

settingItems.description:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, whe
settingItems.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.

For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.
settingItems.label: First layer flow ratio

settingItems.description: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.
settingItems.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer

settingItems.description: Acceleration of the first layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Speed of solid infill part of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer infill

settingItems.description: Jerk for the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer minimum wall width

settingItems.description:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface density

settingItems.description: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.
settingItems.label: Combine brims

settingItems.description: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.
settingItems.label: Use beam interlocking

settingItems.description: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.
settingItems.label: Interlocking depth

settingItems.description: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer expansion

settingItems.description:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.
settingItems.label: Brim ear detection radius

settingItems.description:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.
settingItems.label: Brim ear max angle

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flo
settingItems.label: Brim flow ratio

settingItems.description: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily.
settingItems.label: Brim-object gap

settingItems.description: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.
settingItems.label: Brim type

settingItems.description:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup
settingItems.label: Brim follows compensated outline

settingItems.description: Distance from model to the outermost brim line.
settingItems.label: Brim width

settingItems.description: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.
settingItems.label: Brim width

settingItems.description: Enabling this option means the width of the brim for tree support will be automatically calculated.
settingItems.label: Auto brim width

settingItems.description: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.
settingItems.label: Temperature variation

settingItems.description: When interface-layer temperature boost is active, set the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower so it cools down during the tower.
settingItems.label: Cool down from interface boost during prime tower

settingItems.description: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.
settingItems.label: Enable

settingItems.description:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of
settingItems.label: External

settingItems.description: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree.
settingItems.label: Slow down for overhang

settingItems.description: Speed of the first layer except the solid infill part.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Travel speed of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer travel speed

settingItems.description: Speed of inner wall.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.
settingItems.label: Internal

settingItems.description: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface.
settingItems.label: Internal solid infill

settingItems.description: Print speed of ironing lines.
settingItems.label: Ironing speed

settingItems.description:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightnin
settingItems.label: Alternate extra wall

settingItems.description: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.
settingItems.label: Detect overhang walls

settingItems.description: Detect thin walls which can't contain two line widths, and use single line to print. Maybe not printed very well, because it's not a closed loop.
settingItems.label: Detect thin walls

settingItems.description: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top su
settingItems.label: Infill/Wall overlap

settingItems.description: Acceleration of inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.
settingItems.label: Inner walls

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.
